newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes down $2, Brent trades 18 cts of.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes down $2, Brent trades 18 cts of.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed down $2 a tonne on Friday in dull activity in line with lower U.S. heating oil, traders said.
IPE March gas oil last traded at $162.50 a tonne, 75 cents off the day's high, having moved in a range of $161.75 and $162.75 for the most of the afternoon.
Some traders said they suspected the front month contract's six-week slide could be near to bottoming out.

"The overall downard trend is still intact but I'm still astonished by the way this market is being dragged down. I feel that if it goes much lower you're going to be at risk of a fairly sharp correction," a trader said, noting the contract's $72 per tonne drop since mid-January.
IPE April Brent was trading down 20 cents at $19.15 a barrel at 1751 GMT, 10 cents off the high and in the middle of the day's trading range.
Brent slipped to around $19.08 within 15 minutes of the NYMEX opening before recovering steadily. Support continues to be put at around the $19.09/10 level.
U.S. heating was off 1.73 cents at 54.30 cents a gallon at after sliding below an eight month low for spot heat at 54.55.

Traders in late afternoon continued to cast doubt on talk earlier in the day that April Brent would break below $19 before the end of the session. The last prompt futures fell below that level was August 1 when they posted a $18.79 low.
NYMEX April crude was trading down 29 cents at $20.60 a barrel.
The market appeared unimpressed by an Iraqi statement that it would seek a rise in the amount of oil it may export under an oil-for-food plan in talks with U.N. officials later on Friday.
